title: observability-pipeline-ingestion-debug-notes-priya
content:
Quick scratchpad for ongoing debug of metrics/traces/logs ingestion drop. Mostly a brain dump + commands tried and immediate hypotheses.

Context:
- Symptoms started ~2024-11-02 09:30 UTC after otel-collector restart during config rollout.
- Traces appear to be sampled (Jaeger UI shows very few spans) and many metrics series are missing in prometheus (notably service.cpu_seconds_total and request_duration_seconds for a subset of services).
- Log ingestion shows spikes of 429 from log-forwarder -> s3-ingest-service.
- Affects: hosted-api prod region us-west-2 and canary in us-east-1.
- Related ticket: OBS-4821 (see linked artifacts).

What I validated so far:
- Check collector pods status
  kubectl -n observability get pods -l app=otel-collector
  -> All collectors in Running, one recently restarted (2024-11-02T09:18:04Z)

- Tail collector logs (shortened):
  kubectl -n observability logs otel-collector-7f8b9 -c otel-collector | sed -n '1,200p'
  2024-11-02T09:18:04Z INFO   config_loader.go:112   loading config from /etc/otel-collector/config.yaml
  2024-11-02T09:18:05Z WARN   exporterhelper/queued_retry.go:216  Exporter "prometheusremotewrite" encountered recoverable error; queue is full
  2024-11-02T09:18:06Z ERROR  batchprocessor/batch_processor.go:78  failed to export batch: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = write buffer overflow

- quick grep for ResourceExhausted across collectors -> matches on 3 pods

- Prometheus scrape targets
  curl -sS http://prometheus-service:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.scrapePool=="service-metrics") | {instance:.labels.instance,job:.labels.job,health:.health}'
  -> most targets UP, but ~15% are down/unhealthy (these map to autoscaled pods that recently changed IPs).

- Prom remote_write sidecar (remote-write to metrics pipeline) logs show intermittent 429s and 503s to remote endpoint:
  2024-11-02T09:19:10Z WARN http_client.go:142 remote_write returned status 429
  2024-11-02T09:20:01Z ERROR http_client.go:156 remote_write returned status 503

- Jaeger agent/collector: checked whether sampling config is applied
  kubectl -n observability exec -it jaeger-collector-0 -- cat /etc/jaeger/sampling.json
  -> sampling config present and default=0.001 for a few services; but the dynamic sampling controller shows last update 2024-10-29 (suspicious).

- Logs ingestion path: filebeat -> log-forwarder service -> s3-ingest-service -> s3
  - filebeat: ok, tailing logs, backpressure observed when log-forwarder returns 429.
  - log-forwarder logs: 429 from s3-ingest (rate limit) and occasional 5xx when object size > 5MB.

Commands/experiments tried (and results):
1) Increase collector queue size (temporary)
   - edited config map otel-collector-cm: set memory and queued_retry settings to higher values
   - rolled collectors (kubectl rollout restart daemonset/otel-collector)
   - short-term: reduced ResourceExhausted errors but queues still backpressure after 20m under peak load
   - conclusion: helps but underlying remote endpoint is throttling; need to address downstream capacity/quotas.

2) Re-run sampling controller sync
   - kubectl -n observability delete pod sampling-controller-5d7f9 -> restarted
   - sampling controller logs: ERROR connecting to config-service: timeout; config-service (internal) had transient failure
   - after config-service recovered, sampling rules were re-applied; trace counts improved slightly in canary but not prod.

3) Bypass remote_write to isolate prometheus scrape health
   - temporarily disabled remote_write in prometheus config and restarted prom; local TSDB shows metrics for previously missing series for ~10m but then exporters started dropping since we rely on remote_write for retention/aggregation.
   - shows problem partly at remote_write ingestion endpoint (rate-limited) but also shows short scrape misses mapping to pod churn.

4) Force re-registration of targets (kube-state-metrics restart)
   - restarted kube-state-metrics, scaled down/up a few deployments to trigger new target discovery
   - reduced number of unhealthy scrape targets by ~8; suggests some controller-event backlog caused old IPs to linger.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Otel-collector queues are overloaded because remote backends (metrics remote_write and spans exporter) are throttling (ResourceExhausted/429). Root cause: downstream capacity regression after config change or rollout. Evidence: exporter errors in collector logs and 429/503 on remote endpoints.
- H2: Sampling controller not applying rules due to config-service transient failure -> traces sampled far lower than expected. Evidence: sampling-controller error and sampling.json stale timestamp.
- H3: Service discovery churn (pod IP churn) causing short-term scrape misses causing some metric series to disappear in aggregated views. Evidence: unhealthy scrape targets align with pods that restarted during rollout.
- H4: Log-forwarder hitting S3 ingest rate limits due to batch size change in filebeat or config drift (we saw 5MB object > limit).

Immediate next steps (practical):
- Create short-term mitigation: increase retry/backoff and queue sizes for otel-collector and implement rate-limited fanout to remote_write (reduce concurrency).
- Coordinate with infra-team owning metrics ingestion (cc: Ethan) to check quotas/ingestion capacity on remote cluster (ticket created).
- Reconcile sampling-controller config-service health; add liveness/readiness check to the sampling controller to avoid stale rules.
- Add temporary alert: fraction of spans per minute vs baseline and spike of ResourceExhausted in collector logs -> page on >5% deviation for 15m.
- For logs: adjust filebeat max_bytes to 4MB and retry to avoid oversized objects; add a 429 backoff handler in log-forwarder.

Longer-term:
- Make otel-collector autoscaling for ingestion bursts (horizontal-pod-autoscaler based on queue length metric).
- Harden sampling controller: persisted rules in etcd + push-based updates rather than pulling from config-service only.
- Improve instrumentation: emit collector internal metrics on exporter queue depth and last successful export per exporter.

Outstanding items / TODOs (who):
- Ethan: confirm remote ingestion capacity / any recent config changes on remote_write ingestion cluster (OBS-4821).
- Lena: change filebeat max_bytes and redeploy canary, monitor 429s.
- Priya (me): implement alert and a quick script to scrape collector logs for ResourceExhausted signature and surface to datadog.

Notes / misc snippets:
- collector queue settings we tried: queued_retry:
  - num_workers: "16"
  - queue_size: "50000"
  - enabled: "true"
- Example error snippet for search:
  "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = write buffer overflow"
- Prom remote_write 429 signature: "remote_write returned status 429"

Slack trail: #observability thread "metric ingestion drop" (see linked slack).

If I forget: priority is to stop customer impact in us-west-2 -> temporarily throttle high-cardinality metrics from non-critical services while we stabilize backpressure.

End of notes. Will update as we get more signals.
